page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture with 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 10%. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks and the PassMark memory score also reach top-tier levels. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the average range. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, all placing in the top 25%. Additionally, the CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

This instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency by combining dedicated AMD EPYC processing cores with a large 1920 GB NVMe SSD storage allocation, eliminating the need for separate block storage attachments. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly suitable for relational databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and text processing pipelines. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference workloads, particularly text generation tasks where it achieves strong to top-tier token throughput.
